title: Federal Budget & NDAA Weekly Tracker
description: Fiscal 2027 appropriations, the continuing resolution, NDAA status, reconciliation funds and Golden Dome money.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 9–16. No new appropriations text or NDAA floor vote dated Nov. 13–16 was opened. The Nov. 12 note on Iran-war limits for the Dec. 11 stopgap and the Nov. 11 military construction and Veterans Affairs bill note remain. No new Golden Dome funding bill was found. The NDAA subsection is empty after older items aged out.

items.headline: Senate Democrats want Iran-war funding limits on the Dec. 11 stopgap
items.summary: Roll Call reported Nov. 12 that Sen. Tim Kaine said he is drafting language to end the Iran war and wants it attached to the next continuing resolution, which is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out. Sens. Michael Bennet, Chris Van Hollen, Tammy Duckworth, and Bernie Sanders said they would oppose a deal that does not restrict the administration from using appropriated funds to continue the war. Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray said Democrats are looking at all options, including whether that fight waits until next year. Roll Call said the Office of Management and Budget has not yet sent Congress the anomalies for the stopgap, and that the administration is considering a bill that would run through March.

items.headline: Bloomberg: Senate appropriators release a $173.2 billion military construction and VA bill
items.summary: Bloomberg Government reported Nov. 11 that the Senate Appropriations Committee released, on Tuesday evening, text of a bill to fund military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs, ahead of next month's spending deadline. Bloomberg said the bill would provide $173.2 billion in discretionary funding, according to a summary released by the panel's Republicans. Bloomberg said the committee also released the Agriculture, Food and Drug Administration, and related-agencies bill, and that releasing the bills without a formal Senate markup is a move to advance full-year spending bills.

items.headline: Ars Technica: Golden Dome's $24 billion reconciliation tranche is not in the continuing resolution
items.summary: Ars Technica reported Nov. 9 that Golden Dome's first funding tranche, about $24 billion, was a one-time fiscal 2026 allocation passed through reconciliation, and that the fiscal year ended Oct. 1. Ars said the program's funding dried up last month because the government is operating under a continuing resolution that extends last year's regular military budget and does not include that reconciliation infusion. Ars said the preliminary House and Senate fiscal 2027 bills, if passed as written, would provide only a fraction of the more than $17 billion the administration requested for Golden Dome in this cycle. Ars also said seven House members of the Golden Dome Caucus lost or did not run, including co-chair Rep. Jeff Crank and Rep. Scott DesJarlais, chair of the House subcommittee overseeing Golden Dome, and that Rep. John Garamendi has a path to chair the Strategic Forces subcommittee in January.
